pr_title: Update Discord RPC ranking value depending on the ruleset
pr_body:
- Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/12898
- [x] Update shown ranking depending on ruleset
~Show beatmap star rating~ reverted and will be discussed in #18499
pr_comments: Also not sure if you've read the [relevant issue thread](https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/12898#issuecomment-846404392) but the rank fetching should be ideally extracted to a common component, because it's data that is useful in more places than just this one functionality.

> Also not sure if you've read the [relevant issue thread](https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/12898#issuecomment-846404392) but the rank fetching should be ideally extracted to a common component, because it's data that is useful in more places than just this one functionality.

Yeah I read it and concluded that a simple way of getting the user's statistics would be to use `GetUsersRequest`. As I'm not really familiar to the project structure yet, I didn't know a better way of doing the thing.

I can't get behind this change. You've added one extra API request to a call which is already being made in [at least one other location](https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/42e07b7308c05bd0792ceee0ae691a54f74f8e0d/osu.Game/Beatmaps/DifficultyRecommender.cs#L89-L95) with similar context (current ruleset).

Given that there are multiple usages popping up (and more will likely appear in the future, ie. when we want to show the user's current rank / statistics on the user panel) this lookup and fetch process should be moved out of these individual components into a high level.

Potentially handled by `APIAccess` itself, as that is where the initial population currently happens.

It's going to require a bit more work and thinking, but I think it's better than spamming API requests in individual components like this, as it will require cleaning these up in the future (and potentially the code will be forgotten about until we hit some API limits).

I understood what you said about moving the instructions, but I'm still wondering if I understood it the correct way. Should my modifications be:
1. only client-side : I simply make a call to ``GetUsersRequest`` just after the initial ``GetUserRequest`` has succeeded (because we don't have the ``LocalUser``'s id beforehands)
2. on server-side : create a new type of requests to ressemble the ``GetUsersRequest`` (would be way harder for this "simple" purpose) and be called as ``GetFriendsRequest``

Something that blocks me right now is that ``DiscordRichPresence``'s ``LocalUser.BindValueChanged`` only works one time (excluding the immediate run). As soon as LocalUser has been modified one time, the callback won't work again. Do you know how I should deal with this issue ?

> As soon as `LocalUser` has been modified one time, the callback won't work again

are you sure the local user is actually changing? the local user changes on logout (to a guest user) and on login, after a succcessful user request (to the actual logged in user). i just tested on `master` and it works as expected there.

> > As soon as `LocalUser` has been modified one time, the callback won't work again
> 
> are you sure the local user is actually changing? the local user changes on logout (to a guest user) and on login, after a succcessful user request (to the actual logged in user). i just tested on `master` and it works as expected there.

I've added another request right after ``GetUserRequest`` is successful and when it finishes, it sets ``localUser.Value``, but the callback doesn't trigger
i'm honestly not even sure what you're trying to do at this point so i can't help you. i can't make any sense out of that last comment.

I'm expecting the BindValueChanged event to be triggered (the callback which is set in ``DiscordRichPresence.load()``) each time ``APIAccess.localUser.Value`` is set. But the event is apparently only triggered the first time that ``APIAccess.localUser.Value`` is set (which is in ``APIAccess.run`` when the first ``GetUserRequest`` issued's ``Success`` callback occurs). Though, I'd like to have this event triggered every time ``APIAccess.localUser.Value`` is set
Ok so this is what it would *roughly* look like, I'm not sure about the order of the requests though
The changes in `APIAccess` can be reverted and everything else should work now that user's own profile returns ruleset statistics

issue_context.title: Discord rich presence should show current game mode rank
issue_context.body:
As of now, the discord rich presence shows current game mode, what the user is doing, and his rank
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46694241/119197369-e9280f00-ba87-11eb-868f-9eb2158371f8.png)

The rank shown however, does not reflect the current game mode that is being played, but it shows only osu!std
https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/51e52fffd86347dbdb16c1420d1b3df13debfb1b/osu.Desktop/DiscordRichPresence.cs#L108

Lazer version: 2021.515.0
comments:
Was taking a quick look at getting this one, but seems currently there's no way to get the local user statistics based on the current ruleset. 

One quick way I can think of is making an `IAPIProvider.LocalUserStatistics` and update it based on ruleset changes by refetching via `GetUserRequest()` (with caching and debouncing), but would like to hear if that's fine to do, not sure myself.
If such caching is implemented, note that there are other components (well, looks like just `DifficultyRecommender`) that would benefit from it as well.
Is this the way such a thing is done? I thought we had another way to do it that was implemented recently via `User.RulesetsStatistics`.

The `User.RulesetStatistics` thing is only on `User`s from `UserCompact` responses (i.e. `GetUsersRequest`), if osu!web can also make it exist in regular `User` responses (`GetUserRequest`/`GetFriendRequest`), that would be another good way to fix the OP issue.

review_comments: Also just noticed that this is resolved both to a field here and in to a parameter in `load()` (named `provider`) therein. Would be preferred to rename this field to `provider` and remove the `load()` parameter to unify usage.
